description: Portfolio has grown from 11 to 13 initiatives over recent heartbeats while completion rate remains under 10%. No initiative has ever been completed.

options.label: Moratorium on new initiatives
options.rationale: No new initiatives until swarm-manager-feature-parity completes (3 items left). New ideas as standalone backlog items only. Prevents further dilution.

options.label: No moratorium
options.rationale: Allow new initiatives. Risk: further dilution.

notes: swarm-manager is still relatively new. I’ve been importing initiatives from brainstorming notes outside of swarm-manager, so it’s expected to continue growing its uncompleted initiatives in the short term

topic: Close desktop-monetization-assurance now that rollup is 2/2
description: desktop-monetization-assurance is marked active but both items (execute/lpbs-stripe-monetization-assurance-suite and research/lpbs-payment-guardrails-and-reconciliation-plan) are completed. It has no pending scope in Swarm Manager. Keeping it active misleads portfolio readouts by inflating 'active' count and can make the dashboard treat it as if work remains. Any net-new monetization assurance work already exists in the backlog as independent items (lpbs-payment-anomaly-log-and-alerts, lpbs-checkout-webhook-atomicity, lpbs-upsert-asset-hardcoded-variant-key) and could either stay standalone or be rolled under desktop-release-governance.

options.label: Close initiative
options.rationale: Flip status to completed. Matches current 2/2 rollup. Net-new follow-on work stays standalone or folds into desktop-release-governance.

options.label: Keep active and expand scope
options.rationale: Attach follow-on items (lpbs-payment-anomaly-log-and-alerts, lpbs-checkout-webhook-atomicity, lpbs-upsert-asset-hardcoded-variant-key) so the initiative remains a coherent monetization-assurance umbrella.

options.label: Leave as-is
options.rationale: Accept the status drift; document manually.

notes: Operator wants to keep initiative open for upcoming swarm-manager initiative-level review/follow-up features; plans to perform a review on this one specifically. Decision closed without mutating initiative status. If review surfaces follow-ups, option B (expand scope) becomes the right call at that point.

topic: Resolve initiative edge drift surfaced by swarm-manager overview
description: swarm-manager overview consistency reports 2 missing_explicit edges (child items cross an initiative boundary with no declared parent-initiative dependency) and ~12 possibly_stale edges (declared initiative dependency has no supporting child dependency). Hygiene, not blockers, but unresolved drift erodes trust in the sequencing signal portfolio-manager relies on. Missing_explicit: (1) contribution-outbound-v1-bug-reports -> contribution-settings via execute/contribution-submitter-bug-report, (2) desktop-runtime-interop -> emulator-platform via execute/desktop-ecosystem-interop-regression-coverage. Possibly_stale set spans agent-inbox-unified-retrieval, agent-sandbox-audit-foundation, contribution-inbound-triage, contribution-outbound-extensions, contribution-verification-isolated, decision-visual-grounding-propagation, desktop-release-governance, director-dashboard-gap-workflow, ecosystem-intelligence-loop, and others.

options.label: Add the two missing_explicit edges; keep possibly_stale as-is
options.rationale: Missing edges are real dependencies the graph is hiding. Possibly_stale often reflects architectural (not item-level) dependencies that are legitimately declared only at the initiative level. Minimum-churn fix.

options.label: Add missing + drop all possibly_stale
options.rationale: Treat the graph as strictly item-derived. Aggressive cleanup; risks losing coarse-grained architectural dependencies that never had matching item edges.

options.label: Defer all edge cleanup
options.rationale: Accept drift; revisit when initiative-level dependency mutation tooling lands.

notes: Add the two missing_explicit edges; leave possibly_stale alone. Operator also endorsed a systemic follow-up: run the consistency check on every mutation that could affect edges (item create/edit/move/delete, initiative edit), surface drift delta on API/CLI/UI response with a suggested one-step fix, and add a vetted mark for legitimately architectural possibly_stale edges so they stop being repeat noise. Captured for backlog in Phase 8.
